data.name: The Technomancer
data.detailed_description:
The Technomancer is a sci-fi RPG set on Mars, featuring dynamic combat and an epic story line, where your choices will affect the fate of the Red Planet. You are a Technomancer, a formidable warrior harnessing destructive electrical powers. Embark on a perilous journey across a planet torn apart by conflict and infested with mutant creatures.

Travel with your companions, choosing between diplomacy, combat or trickery to resolve quests. Gain experience to level up your character, and learn new skills or upgrade perks across 4 unique skill trees. Loot, buy and craft more powerful equipment and weaponry for yourself and teammates, to stand a chance of surviving!

Only you can forge the destiny of Mars.


  • An adventure set on the terraformed deserts of a post-apocalyptic Red Planet
  • Three combat styles with deep character customization
  • Unleash powerful Technomancy abilities on your foes
  • In-depth crafting changes the appearance and stats of weapons and armour
  • A world that reacts to your decisions
  • Relationships with your companions open new pathways and quests

reviews.review:
[h1]Kill a fellow unfortunate and, in this hell, only the more alone we will become...[/h1]

After finishing Mars: War Logs, I had to play this game next and fell back in love with the setting and lore. The Technomancer serves as a prequel that begins before Mars: War Logs, but the two games eventually run in parallel as their stories unfold in this post-apocalyptic setting. 

You play as Zachariah Rouge, an Abundance Technomancer in the making, as your first mission is to finish your initiation to become an official Technomancer. The mission was not an easy one, as your master, Sean Mancer, showed you the biggest secret of all Technomancers; the source of their power. You had to give an oath to keep, as well as find the Earth. After this initiation and ceremony, your name changes to Zachariah Mancer. In Aurora, people's names are virtues. In Abundance, each person's last name relates to their job. 
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3829455304

You'll be assigned as a lieutenant, and that's when things go south for you in the corporate city of Ophir, where you'll be cast out and begin your journey to find shelter and people to help you against the man who will not stop until he gets the secret from you. Besides that, there is the ultimate goal of finding the Earth.

If you have played any of Spider's games, you'll be familiar with the action combat and skill trees. You'll be able to switch between four classes during combat. A tank, a rogue with guns and daggers, a lancer, and, of course, electricity magic as a Technomancer.  You can upgrade each class in their designated skill trees and upgrade your talents. I found that science and charisma are very important, as they unlock extra dialogue options that let you convince people around you. 
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3829457619

Speaking of people, you do have a reputation you must balance, or even the companions who were willing to help you might leave you. This part was tricky for me because not everyone can be happy with your actions even if you think you did the right thing. There are five factions that can drop to hostile or become friendly with you. There are three romance options for you, and there are no gender restrictions, since you can only be a male character. And just like in the previous game, killing people will severely affect your Karma, and people will start fearing you. 

The quests were not bad but require a lot of backtracking; the worst part is that enemies respawn quickly, and with the clunky, slow combat, you could die. Aside from that, I liked the atmosphere and graphics of the three main cities; you can fast-travel between them from a specific area where you park your vehicle, and you can switch between companions. Bringing the right companion to the right place will give you the upper hand when negotiating with others. 

The graphics were good, and the character design has improved compared to the previous game, as you can tell from the return of some characters. They do look good despite the lack of facial emotions, and the area details are nice, especially the second and third major cities you'll visit. The soundtracks grew on me, and I enjoyed them a lot while playing. 
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3829767980

Some of the voice acting was lacking, but most of the characters are likable. I liked the main character; you can see his personality change as he makes moral decisions, and there are a lot of those. 

Pros:
+Great story. (A prequel to Mars: War Logs)
+Choices have real consequences with moral choices.
+Switching classes and crafting mid-battle.
+Companions and romance.
+Great soundtracks.
+Good voice-overs, but some are mediocre and lack emotion (Game is fully voiced)
+Multiple endings. (You choose sides and decide a major event)
+Unlimited manual saves.
+Fast traveling to major cities.
+Cutscenes and dialogues are skippable.
+Steam achievements.

Cons:
-Lots of backtracking.
-Slow combat.


The first two chapters were amazing, but the last one felt rushed compared to them. I wish they added more climactic events in it.  I don't mind low-budget games at all, and I keep that in mind during gameplay to enjoy them. Recommended.
